Share SOC2 report + private deployment network diagram

Ethan Park - send pricing tiers and pilot contract template (due 2025-12-05)

header: Date: 2025-12-03 | Start: 15:00 PST | Duration: 48 mins | Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Priya Ramesh (Redwood SE), Maya Li (Redwood CSM); Sam Torres (Helio Head of ML), Nina Alvarez (Helio Platform), Jon Park (Helio CTO)
summary: Redwood demo of Optimize console focusing on quantization profile comparisons (INT8 vs FP8). SE walked through per-prompt quality delta, latency histograms, and cost tradeoffs. Customer requested benchmarks on their prompt set, SOC2 + private deployment docs, and a two-week dedicated pilot. Action items assigned for profile sweeps and contract/pricing delivery.
transcript:
[00:00] Ethan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep this to about 45 minutes and show the Optimize console quant profile comparisons. I know Helio's focused on retail responses where latency at checkout is critical.
[00:12] Sam (Helio): Yep, thanks. Our main asks are: keep 95th percentile under 200ms and don't degrade NPS on generative suggestions.
[00:25] Priya (Redwood SE): Great. Quick agenda: demo Optimize live, show INT8 vs FP8 profiles, per-prompt quality delta, cost model, then Q&A and next steps.
[00:35] Nina (Helio): Quick note — we run in us-west and have a VPC requirement, likely Dedicated or Private.
[00:40] Priya: Understood. We'll show both hosted fallback and Dedicated latency curves. Opening the console now — bear with me, it's a little slow.
[01:12] Priya: (screen) So this is the Optimize -> Profiles page. On the left you can see saved quant profiles; we've loaded two for this demo: redwood-int8-retail and redwood-fp8-lowlat. The compare view lets you pick a prompt set; I'm uploading a small sample of Helio retail prompts.
[01:35] Sam: The upload is anonymized, FYI.
[01:40] Priya: Yep, good. Running a 100-query sweep across both profiles. Note that INT8 gives a 2.6x token throughput improvement on our infra but we often see a 0.8 - 1.5 point BLEU-like quality drop on some instruction-following prompts.
[02:05] Jon (Helio): When you say "BLEU-like" are you using a specific metric? We mostly use Rouge/ROUGE-L + human labels.
[02:12] Priya: Good call — for retail suggestions we compute a composite quality score: semantic-accuracy + brand-safety + human label percentage. In the console I show a per-prompt delta and a distribution chart.
[02:28] Priya: Alright results are in... interesting. INT8 shows median latency 85ms, p95 210ms. FP8 shows median 120ms, p95 320ms. Quality delta: for our sample, average quality drop for INT8 vs FP8 is -1.2 points, but 8 prompts (out of 100) had >3 point drop.
[02:55] Sam: Those 8 prompts — can we get examples? The edge cases matter if they impact checkout suggestions.
[03:02] Priya: Yep, we can export the flagged prompts. (murmur) exporting... done, link in chat. Note: console shows per-prompt example outputs; transcriptions of product names occasionally garble — sorry speech-to-text.
[03:20] Maya (Redwood CSM): I'll attach that export to the follow-up email.
[03:25] Priya: Also, Optimize shows a suggestion: enable prefix KV caching for those prompts with long shared prefixes, and enable mixed-precision for attention kernels. That often reduces token compute on FP8 without affecting quality.
[03:43] Nina: Is mixed-precision safe in Private deployments? We require HSM KMS and no egress.
[03:49] Priya: Yes — that's a runtime config. Private deployment preserves all network controls; mixed-precision is purely compute-level, no data leaves. We'll also provide an architecture diagram.
[04:05] Sam: What's the unit-cost delta? If INT8 is faster, is it always cheaper?
[04:09] Priya: Not always. INT8 reduces GPU memory and increases throughput, but if you need frequent model fallbacks or run more post-processing you can lose savings. Console has a cost calculator — I'm switching to Cost Simulator.
[04:30] Priya: For this sample, INT8 reduces per-1k-token cost by ~38% on Hosted; on Dedicated it's ~30% because reserved pricing changes the amortization. FP8 gives slightly higher cost but fewer quality regressions.
[04:50] Jon: Could we do a hybrid: INT8 for low-risk prompts and FP8 for branded/product-name prompts?
[04:56] Ethan: Absolutely — Optimize supports route-based profiles: you can route by prompt fingerprint, route by endpoint, or by customer segment. We can do canary rollouts too.
[05:08] Sam: How do you fingerprint prompts? We have templated prompts with variable slots.
[05:13] Priya: We compute a canonicalized hash after stripping slot tokens; the console shows grouping and frequency. You can make policies like "if group frequency > 0.01 and contains product_token then use FP8."
[05:28] Nina: That sounds helpful. What about cold-starts for KV cache? Our live traffic has lots of unique sessions at peak.
[05:35] Priya: Good point — cold cache increases latency. For Dedicated we recommend warmers during traffic ramp; the console's Autoscale + warm-up policy can pre-fill caches from historical traces.
[05:46] Sam: Any known gotchas with accuracy drift over time when using INT8?
[05:51] Priya: Drift can appear if you update tokenizers or model variants; Optimize has continuous evals — you can attach a small labeled eval set and get regression alerts.
[06:05] Ethan: I'll show the regression alerts tab — here's an example where INT8 started showing a drop after a minor model patch. You can auto-roll back to FP8 on a threshold.
[06:22] Nina: Nice. Can we pin a model version in Dedicated but change quant profiles without redeploy?
[06:27] Priya: Yes — profiles are orthogonal to model version; kernel selection happens at runtime.
[06:33] Jon: Can you run the same sample against our on-prem infra during the pilot? We have DGX boxes.
[06:39] Priya: We can run an offline benchmark runner that you execute on-prem; we'll provide a runner container and a small harness. Results can be uploaded to Optimize for side-by-side comparison.
[06:52] Sam: So next steps would be: we send Helio prompt set, Redwood runs a full 2k prompt sweep on both profiles and shares the spreadsheet?
[06:59] Ethan: Yep, we'll include latencies, per-prompt diffs, and kernel-level traces.
[07:05] Priya: One more demo bit — console shows a stacked latency histogram, with tokenization and attention kernel breakdown. You can see INT8 reduces attention kernel time but increases softmax variance slightly.
[07:20] Sam: The variance — does that affect p99 often?
[07:23] Priya: It can. That's why we recommend p95/p99 SLO checks and setting fallback policies: if p95 goes above threshold, route to FP8 automatically.
[07:34] Jon: How is quantization handled for multi-turn chat with KV cache? Does INT8 preserve cache keys?
[07:40] Priya: Yes, KV cache format is stable — we do quant-aware cache packing. The console warns if quant switch would require cache rebuild; Optimize can perform live cache migration or do a cold-start depending on policy.
[07:55] Nina: Any security notes for the pilot? We need audit logs and SSO via SAML.
[08:00] Maya (CSM): We will share audit log options and SAML setup doc. For Private we can also enable customer-managed KMS.
[08:10] Sam: Good. Quick question on quality measurement: can we have human-in-the-loop labeling via console?
[08:15] Priya: Yes — there's an evaluation workspace where you can surface model responses, queue them for human review, and write simple rubric checks. We can integrate with Helio's existing labeling tool via API.
[08:28] Sam: Perfect. Any data residency concerns?
[08:31] Ethan: We support region pinning and on-prem for stricter needs. We'll include region endpoints in the pilot plan.
[08:40] Priya: Alright I'll pause demo for Q&A...
[08:45] Jon: Two quick things: 1) For the examples that degraded >3 points, can you reproduce deterministically on our DGX? 2) What's the rollback latency if we detect quality regression?
[08:56] Priya: Reproducible runs are possible with the harness. Rollback in the console is near-instant for routing; full traffic flip can be staged over minutes depending on traffic — we recommend canary windows.
[09:10] Sam: Ok that works.
[09:12] Ethan: Recap of action items: Priya will run the profile sweep on Helio prompts; Ethan sends pricing and contract; Sam will share 200 prompts + labeling. We'll also schedule pilot kickoff next week.
[09:28] Nina: One last micro question — do you support FP8 mantissa variants? We heard some runtimes call it e4m3 vs e5m2.
[09:34] Priya: Yes, Optimize abstracts those as FP8 variants; console shows accuracy impact per mantissa choice. We'll include that in the sweep.
[09:44] Sam: Great — thanks everyone.
[09:46] Ethan: Thanks, we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and SOC2 docs. Bye.
[09:50] (call ends)
